title: Axial T1 — hip and proximal thigh
region: Hemipelvis, hip joint and proximal thigh
sideNote: Side not confirmed from the screen recording. No L or R marker is visible on the images; the only orientation marker present is P (posterior), at the foot of each slice.
provenance: Reconstructed from a screen recording: 321 frames reduced to 173 distinct images by collapsing held frames, ordered anatomically by spectral seriation of the slice-similarity graph with 2-opt refinement, then merged to 38 unique levels. Frame order in the recording is not slice order — the reader scrolled back over the same anatomy twice.

structures.name: Femoral head
structures.recognition: The only large sphere in the section: uniformly bright fatty marrow inside a thin, uniformly dark cortical rim, sitting in the acetabular cup. On T1 its marrow signal should match the greater trochanter and the shaft.

structures.name: Acetabulum
structures.recognition: The C-shaped socket medial to the head. On an axial slice you see it as anterior and posterior walls with the joint space between them and the head; the posterior wall is the thicker of the two.

structures.name: Femoral neck
structures.recognition: The marrow-filled bar running posterolaterally from the head toward the trochanter. Follow it down the stack: the head becomes an oval, then a bar, then merges with the trochanteric mass.

structures.name: Greater trochanter
structures.recognition: The lateral marrow-containing prominence with the gluteal tendons converging on it. It appears lateral to the neck and is the most lateral bone in the section.

structures.name: Proximal femoral shaft
structures.recognition: A thick black ring of cortex with bright fatty marrow inside — the densest black on a T1 thigh. Everything else in the thigh is arranged around it.

structures.name: Gluteus maximus
structures.origin: Posterior gluteal line of the ilium, dorsal sacrum and coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament
structures.insertion: Iliotibial tract and the gluteal tuberosity of the femur
structures.action: Extension and external rotation of the hip; its upper fibres abduct
structures.recognition: The most superficial and most posterior muscle in every slice from the pelvis down — it forms the whole back of the section, immediately deep to subcutaneous fat.

structures.name: Gluteus medius
structures.origin: Outer surface of the ilium between the posterior and anterior gluteal lines
structures.insertion: Lateral facet of the greater trochanter
structures.action: Hip abduction; anterior fibres internally rotate. Holds the pelvis level in single-leg stance
structures.recognition: Lateral, and superficial to gluteus minimus — the pair look like two shells wrapped round the outer ilium, medius the outer one. Trace them down and both converge as tendons on the greater trochanter.

structures.name: Gluteus minimus
structures.origin: Outer ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines
structures.insertion: Anterior facet of the greater trochanter
structures.recognition: The deeper of the two — it lies directly on the outer table of the ilium with gluteus medius outside it, separated by a thin fat plane. If you can see bone touching muscle with no muscle between, that muscle is minimus.

structures.name: Tensor fasciae latae
structures.origin: Anterior part of the outer lip of the iliac crest and the anterior superior iliac spine
structures.action: Assists hip abduction and internal rotation; tenses the iliotibial tract
structures.recognition: A small anterolateral muscle sitting right under the skin at the front-outer corner of the section. Follow it down and it disappears into the iliotibial band while sartorius runs the opposite way, medially.

structures.name: Sartorius
structures.insertion: Pes anserinus, on the medial surface of the proximal tibia
structures.action: Flexes, abducts and externally rotates the hip; flexes the knee
structures.recognition: A small, flat, strap-like muscle just under the skin that migrates medially as you scroll down — it starts near the anterior superior iliac spine and crosses the front of the thigh to the medial side. It forms the lateral border of the femoral triangle, and further down it roofs the adductor canal. It is sartorius, never serratus.

structures.name: Rectus femoris
structures.origin: Direct head from the anterior inferior iliac spine; reflected head from the supra-acetabular groove
structures.insertion: Quadriceps tendon to the patella, then the tibial tuberosity via the patellar ligament
structures.action: Extends the knee and flexes the hip — the only quadriceps head that crosses both joints
structures.recognition: The most anterior and superficial of the quadriceps, oval in cross-section, sitting on top of vastus intermedius. Near the hip it is a tendon at the anterior inferior iliac spine; it only becomes a belly further down.

structures.name: Vastus lateralis
structures.origin: Greater trochanter, intertrochanteric line and lateral lip of the linea aspera
structures.insertion: Quadriceps tendon and the lateral patella
structures.recognition: The bulk of the lateral thigh, lying directly deep to the iliotibial band and wrapping the lateral cortex of the femur.

structures.name: Vastus intermedius
structures.origin: Anterior and lateral surfaces of the femoral shaft
structures.recognition: The layer sandwiched between rectus femoris and the front of the femur — it is the quadriceps head lying directly on the bone.

structures.name: Iliopsoas
structures.origin: Psoas major from T12–L5 vertebral bodies and transverse processes; iliacus from the iliac fossa
structures.innervation: Psoas major, anterior rami L1–L3; iliacus, femoral nerve (L2, L3)
structures.recognition: Sits directly in front of the hip joint, between the femoral vessels medially and the anterior acetabulum behind. Scroll down and it narrows into a tendon that heads for the lesser trochanter — that is the moment psoas and iliacus have fused.

structures.name: Adductor longus
structures.origin: Anterior body of the pubis, below the pubic crest
structures.insertion: Middle third of the linea aspera
structures.innervation: Obturator nerve, anterior division (L2, L3, L4)
structures.action: Adducts and assists flexion of the hip
structures.recognition: The most anterior and most superficial of the adductor group, forming the medial border of the femoral triangle. Depth is the key: longus in front, brevis behind it, magnus behind that.

structures.name: Adductor magnus
structures.origin: Inferior pubic ramus, ischial ramus and ischial tuberosity
structures.insertion: Linea aspera and the adductor tubercle of the femur
structures.innervation: Obturator nerve, and the tibial division of the sciatic nerve for the hamstring part
structures.action: Powerful hip adduction; the hamstring part extends the hip
structures.recognition: The largest and most posterior of the adductors, forming a broad sheet between the adductor group in front and the hamstrings behind.

structures.name: Gracilis
structures.origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis
structures.insertion: Pes anserinus, on the medial proximal tibia
structures.action: Adducts the hip and flexes the knee
structures.recognition: The thin strap right at the medial edge of the thigh, immediately under the skin — the most medial muscle in the section at every level.

structures.name: Hamstring origin (common tendon)
structures.innervation: Sciatic nerve (tibial division; short head of biceps from the common peroneal division)
structures.recognition: A dark, low-signal tendinous mass on the back of the ischial tuberosity, deep to gluteus maximus. Semimembranosus arises anterolaterally on the tuberosity, and semitendinosus with the biceps long head share a conjoint tendon posteromedially.

structures.name: Sciatic nerve
structures.action: Motor to the hamstrings and everything below the knee; sensory to most of the leg and foot
structures.recognition: A flat, ovoid, slightly striated structure lying in fat between the ischium and gluteus maximus, then running behind adductor magnus in the thigh. It is larger than any vessel at this level and does not have a flow void.

structures.name: Femoral vessels
structures.recognition: Paired round low-signal structures in the fat of the femoral triangle, anteromedial to iliopsoas. Artery and vein cannot be separated with confidence on this study, so they are labelled together.
structures.note: Labelled as a pair deliberately. On this recording the artery and vein cannot be told apart reliably, and guessing which is which would be inventing a finding.

structures.name: Iliotibial band
structures.recognition: A hairline of very low signal hugging the lateral margin of the thigh, superficial to vastus lateralis. It is the thickened lateral part of the fascia lata, and receives tensor fasciae latae and part of gluteus maximus.

structures.name: Subcutaneous fat
structures.recognition: The bright rind around the whole section. On T1 fat is the brightest tissue there is, which is what makes this a T1 image: were this fat-suppressed, this rind would be black.
